title: The MS Warrior: Reclaiming Your Life from Uncertainty
summary: A fierce, compassionate, and scientifically grounded program designed to help you navigate the unpredictable storms of Multiple Sclerosis. This is not just about coping; it is about reclaiming your identity from the disease. We combine advanced neuro-psychoeducation with cognitive behavioral strategies to combat fatigue, master uncertainty, and rewire your mindset for resilience.

modules.title: Module 1 • The Biology of the Beast: Understanding Your Body
modules.overview: To fight your enemy, you must understand it. MS is not 'in your head'—it is in your nerves. This module provides world-class psychoeducation on what is happening inside your Central Nervous System (CNS). We validate the invisible symptoms. That 'brain fog' and that leaden exhaustion? They are biological short-circuits, not character flaws. We begin the journey of shifting from a 'victim of diagnosis' to the 'pilot of a complex machine.'
takeaways: Demyelination is like a frayed electrical wire; the signal is trying to get through, but it's static.
Your fatigue is biological (primary MS fatigue), not just 'being tired.'
You are not your lesions. You are the consciousness navigating them.
exercises: Symptom Validation Map: Draw a body map. Mark the invisible symptoms (numbness, heat sensitivity, fatigue) that others don't see. Own them.
The 'Not My Fault' List: Write down three symptoms you often blame yourself for (e.g., 'laziness') and re-label them correctly (e.g., 'primary fatigue').
homework: The Biology Review: Explain the 'frayed wire' analogy to one trusted person in your life this week to practice communicating your reality.

modules.title: Module 2 • The Energy Economy: Mastering MS Fatigue
modules.overview: Fatigue is the most debilitating symptom of MS. It is not sleepiness; it is a power failure. This module teaches you to become an elite economist of your own energy. We introduce 'The Spoon Theory' and CBT Pacing. You will learn to stop the 'Boom and Bust' cycle where you do too much on good days and crash for three days after. Rest is not laziness. In the world of MS, rest is a weapon. It is a strategic recharge.
takeaways: The 'Boom and Bust' cycle destroys your stamina; consistency builds it.
You have a limited energy budget every day. Spend it like gold.
Strategic Rest (pre-emptive resting) prevents the crash.
exercises: Energy Audit: Track your activities for one day. Assign a 'Spoon Cost' to each. Did you go over budget?
The 45/15 Rule: Try working/doing chores for 45 minutes, then forcing a 15-minute rest (no phone, eyes closed) *before* you feel tired.
homework: The 'No' Challenge: Say 'no' to one non-essential demand this week to save a spoon for something you actually love.

modules.title: Module 3 • Rewiring the Mind: Grief and Cognitive Adaptation
modules.overview: MS involves loss. Loss of mobility, loss of certainty, loss of the 'old you.' It is crucial to grieve, but dangerous to get stuck in the grief. This module applies Cognitive Restructuring to the dark thoughts that come with chronic illness: 'I am a burden,' 'I am broken,' 'My life is over.' We fight the neurological damage with psychological neuroplasticity. We cannot fix the myelin, but we can upgrade the mindset.
takeaways: Grief is not linear; it is a spiral. Allow yourself to feel it.
Thoughts are not facts. 'I can't do this' is a feeling, not a prophecy.
Focus on 'Can Do' vs. 'Can't Do' without toxic positivity.
exercises: The Thought Record: Catch a negative thought (e.g., 'I am useless'). Write down the evidence *against* it (e.g., 'I listened to my friend today, I finished a project').
Values Alignment: List 3 core values (e.g., Kindness, Creativity). List how you can express them *even with* MS symptoms.
homework: Grief Letter: Write a letter to your diagnosis. Scream at it, cry at it, thank it for the lessons. Get it all out on paper.

modules.title: Module 4 • Dancing with Uncertainty: Managing Anxiety
modules.overview: MS is the disease of 'What If?' What if I relapse? What if I need a wheelchair? This uncertainty is a heavy psychological torment. This module teaches you to tolerate uncertainty. We use mindfulness and grounding to pull you out of the terrifying future and back into the manageable present. You will learn to distinguish between 'Prudent Preparation' and 'Catastrophic Worrying.'
takeaways: Worrying about a relapse does not prevent it; it only ruins today.
Hyper-vigilance (scanning your body for symptoms) amplifies pain.
Control what you can (diet, sleep, stress); surrender the rest.
exercises: The 'What If' vs. 'Then I Will' Game: For every scary 'What If' thought, write a practical 'Then I Will' plan. (e.g., 'What if I can't drive?' -> 'Then I will use ride-share and save on insurance').
5-4-3-2-1 Grounding: When fear hits, name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste.
homework: Worry Time: Set a timer for 15 minutes a day. You are allowed to worry as hard as you want. When the timer goes off, worry time is over. Go live.

modules.title: Module 5 • Defiant Adaptation: Problem-Solving for Mobility
modules.overview: Adaptation is not surrender. Adaptation is defiance. It is saying, 'I will do this, even if I have to do it differently.' This module uses the 'Selection, Optimization, and Compensation' (SOC) model. We tackle physical limitations with a problem-solving engineer's mindset. We address the shame of using assistive devices (canes, scooters) and reframe them as tools of liberation.
takeaways: A cane is not a symbol of weakness; it is a tool for freedom.
Doing it differently is better than not doing it at all.
Focus on the *function*, not the *method*.
exercises: The Obstacle Course: Pick one activity you have stopped doing (e.g., gardening). Brainstorm 3 ways to adapt it so you can do it (e.g., raised beds, sitting, early morning).
Tool Test: Go to a medical supply store or look online. Find one tool that would make your life 10% easier. Commit to trying it.
homework: The 'Yes, And' Experiment: Do an activity differently. Tell yourself, 'I am doing this differently, AND I am enjoying it.'

modules.title: Module 6 • You Are More Than Your CNS: Identity & Relationships
modules.overview: MS can feel like it swallows your whole identity. You become 'The Patient.' This module is about reclaiming your role as a partner, parent, professional, and lover. We tackle the difficult conversations: how to explain invisible symptoms to family, how to handle intimacy when your body feels numb or tired, and how to set boundaries without guilt. You are a person who *has* MS. You are not MS.
takeaways: Communication bridges the gap between your invisible reality and their visible world.
Intimacy may need adaptation, but connection is always possible.
You have value beyond your physical productivity.
exercises: The 'Who Am I?' Wheel: Draw a pie chart of your identity. 'MS Patient' can be a slice, but it cannot be the whole pie. Fill in the rest (Friend, Reader, Joker).
The Script: Write a script to explain a specific symptom to a specific person who 'doesn't get it.'
homework: Intimacy Date: Plan a moment of connection with a partner or friend that requires zero physical energy (e.g., listening to music together, cuddling, audiobooks).

modules.title: Module 7 • The Unbreakable Spirit: Resilience & The Future
modules.overview: You have the tools. You understand the biology. You have grieved, adapted, and paced. Now, we build the fortress for the future. This final module is about 'Resilience Planning.' We prepare a 'Relapse Drill' so that if the storm comes back, you don't panic—you execute the plan. We celebrate the Warrior Spirit. You are surviving something difficult every single day. That deserves applause.
takeaways: Resilience is not bouncing back; it's bouncing forward.
A Relapse Plan reduces the trauma of a flare-up.
You are the expert on your body and your life.
exercises: The Relapse Action Plan: Write it down. Laminate it. Put it on the fridge.
Victory Log: Write down 5 things you have achieved *since* your diagnosis. Proof that life continues.
homework: The Manifesto: Write a short personal mission statement for your life with MS. (e.g., 'I will pace myself, I will respect my body, and I will not apologize for my needs').

aiSupport.systemPrompt: Help the user apply one concrete module step at a time. Do not diagnose. Escalate urgent safety concerns to emergency care.
